messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT created: SLO breach for /v1/generate (p99 > 2s). Triggered at 2026-02-28T12:09:03Z. Paging on-call.

maria: i'm on-call, looking at traces + metrics now. initial alert shows p95 and p99 climbing for the past 7m.

raj: infra view — control-plane DB (auth/config) connections spiking. RPS on config_fetch up 6x, error rate to config-service ~4%. DB slow queries visible.

hao: runtime traces show streaming tail stalls where the model worker is waiting on "config-fetch"/auth lookup before continuing KV cache restore. pattern: many short-lived control-plane calls per request.

leni: seeing repeated 429s and 5xx from feature-flag-service to control-plane, lots of retries. looks like cascade: ff-service -> config-service -> DB.

maria: customer impact: several high-volume customers experiencing streaming stalls (clients see chunk gaps), a few 503s. marking P1.

simon: product note — affected endpoints: streaming generate and chat streaming only, non-streaming completions a little slower but functional.

raj: quick metrics snapshot: p95 (/v1/generate) baseline ~120ms -> 820ms; p99 baseline ~420ms -> 2.8s. control-plane latency 99th ~1.4s.

maria: can we confirm origin? is this auth DB hot partition or an app-level config stampede?

hao: traces show identical stack: model-proxy calls /control/config?customer_id with no TTL hit, then waits. config-service logs show many full-cache misses. suspect cache TTL mis-config or a recent deploy that disabled local caching.

leni: remembered a deploy ~10m before spike: deploy-bot: "deploy config-service v2.3.7" — new config change toggled FEATURE_CACHE_LOCAL=false in canary.

maria: ok — rollback or flip that flag? we should prefer non-breaking mitigations first.

raj: immediate mitigations I can do now: increase DB connection pool size for config-service, add short-lived read replica route, and reduce control-plane request retries. doing in parallel.

maria: hao, can runtime side avoid sync config fetch on hot path? even temporary bypass to use last-known static config?

hao: yes. adding an emergency fallback: model-proxy will use local static config if control-plane call > 300ms or returns error. pushing a global env toggle now: FEATURE_FLAG_FALLBACK=static.

maria: command for fallback toggle:

```
kubectl set env deployment/model-proxy FEATURE_FLAG_FALLBACK=static -n prod
```

deploy-bot: rollout started for deployment/model-proxy (3 pods at a time).

raj: DB pool increased, lowered max retries on control-plane client from 5 -> 2. Also applied query timeout enforcement on config-service to fail fast.

leni: re-enabled local ff cache on canary nodes (TTL=30m) via:

```
kubectl patch deployment feature-flag-service -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"ff","env":[{"name":"FEATURE_CACHE_LOCAL","value":"true"},{"name":"FF_CACHE_TTL","value":"1800"}]}]}}}}'
```

maria: results?

raj: within 90s p95 dropped to ~360ms, p99 down to ~1.1s. control-plane error rate back to ~0.5%.

hao: streaming stalls reduced, tail latency improved. a few residual 503s while pods finish rolling.

maria: coordinating customer comms — simon can you draft a short note? mention mitigation and ETA for full recovery.

simon: drafted. will post to status.redwood.ai when we confirm stable for 15m.

maria: next steps: 1) keep fallback enabled for 1h, 2) rollback the canary change that set FEATURE_CACHE_LOCAL=false (we'll revert the config-service change), 3) run postmortem to determine why deploy flipped cache off without perf guardrails.

raj: started rollback for config-service canary to v2.3.6. command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/config-service --to-revision=45`

deploy-bot: config-service rollout undo commenced.

leni: extra: added temporary circuit-breaker on model-proxy for config calls to fail open after 3 consecutive timeouts (30s window).

maria: good. handing off to hao for next 45m while i take owner notification calls and prepare incident bridge notes. please @maria if anything regresses.

hao: taking over. i'll monitor traces and scaling. planning to keep FEATURE_FLAG_FALLBACK=static until full rollback completes and we validate stable for 30m.

maria: on-call handoff: status: mitigations applied, p99 trending down. impact: streaming stalls affecting a subset of customers, reduced after fixes. action items assigned to raj (DB + config-service rollback), hao (runtime fallback + monitor), leni (ff cache revocation audit), simon (customer comms).

hao: will also add a smoke-check job to hit streaming generate every 30s across regions to detect regressions quickly.

maria: ETA for full recovery? aiming 30-45m, will update status page when stable for 15m.

raj: config-service rollback complete, healthchecks green. DB metrics are back to normal.

hao: observed stable p95 ~150ms, p99 ~420ms for past 12m. moving to monitoring mode.

maria: closing active paging but leaving incident open for postmortem. final impact: brief SLO breach (p99 >2s) for ~12min, streaming stalls for subset of customers, root cause: config-cache disabled by canary deploy leading to load on config-service and DB, causing tail latency in inference path.

simon: status update posted to status.redwood.ai, customers notified.

maria: excellent work. assign postmortem to eng-runtime + eng-sre. include timeline, deploy guard, and automated rollback criteria for cache toggles.

hao: noted — will start draft postmortem.

maria: handing off final ownership to raj for remediation follow-ups. i'll be available for blameless review. :white_check_mark:
